prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts a breakroom and adjacent hallway as the camera wearer walks forward and turns left and right across the five frames, starting outside a doorway (~1.5–2 m on the right in frame 1) looking at distant tables and refrigerators (~4–6 m away). In frames 2 and 4, a wooden snack counter sits ~2–4 m in front and to the left of the camera wearer with a small table and chairs ~2.5–3 m to the right in frame 2, while in frame 3 a white shelving unit on the left is within arm's reach (~0.5–1.5 m) and separates the breakroom from the dark hallway receding >8 m straight ahead. A standing man in a dark shirt and khaki trousers stands just behind the wooden counter (within arm's reach of the counter at <0.5 m), positioned ~4–5 m away in frame 2, ~3–4 m on the far right in frame 3, ~3 m to the left of the counter in frame 4, and ~1.5–2 m on the right in frame 5 alongside trash bins ~1.5–3 m on the left; throughout, he faces rightward in profile away from the camera wearer while the lower half of his body is occluded by the counter in frames 2–4, and a second person's leg appears partly in view at the far right edge of frame 5 (<1.5 m away). Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the near doorway wall in frame 1, the foreground snack shelf in frame 3, and the continuous ground-plane distance gradient down the dark painted hallway, though it is unreliable on the distant person in frame 2 (blending him into the dark background wall) and flattens fine shelf items and glass display cases into solid blocks.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates selected foreground and mid-ground objects across the breakroom and hallway, leaving most of the scene layout unlabelled in black. In frame 1 no instances are detected due to motion blur, whereas frame 2 places a green 'chair' (~2.5 m away) in front of a purple 'person' mask (~3 m away, actually a grey chair by the table) and a pink 'tv' mask (~4.5 m away, actually the glass-door refrigerator), with a light-green 'tv' (the countertop display case, ~3.5 m away) and 'book' (snack rack) ~2 m to their left. In frame 3, a large cyan 'refrigerator' mask covers the close white snack shelves on the left (~0.5–1.5 m away, within the camera wearer's arm's reach) while the standing man is detected as a brown 'person' mask ~3.5–4 m to the right behind the counter, facing right and not looking at the camera wearer; in frame 4, as the camera turns right, this same man appears ~3 m away on the left next to a yellow 'bottle' and green 'tv' mask (display case, ~2–2.5 m away, within the man's arm's reach). By frame 5, as the camera approaches the hallway, the standing man is fully segmented in pink on the right at ~1.5–2 m facing right toward a second brown 'person' mask (<1.5 m away, partly out of view at the right edge and occluded by the foreground counter). While segmentation highlights the occluded lower-limb sliver of the man behind the counter in frame 4 and the partially visible second person's leg in frame 5 that are easy to miss in RGB, it is highly unreliable for class labels—misclassifying refrigerators and display cases as 'tv', shelves as 'refrigerator', and a chair as 'person'—and completely misses the standing man in frame 2 as well as the wooden counters and trash bins.
descriptions.pose: The body/hand skeleton map tracks only the standing man on the right side of the hallway and counter in frames 3, 4, and 5, providing no scene layout or object geometry and detecting nothing in frames 1 and 2. As the camera wearer approaches from ~3.5–4 m in frame 3 to ~3 m in frame 4 and ~1.5–2 m in frame 5, the yellow body skeleton shifts from the far right (frame 3) toward the center-left (frame 4) and back to the right (frame 5) as the camera pans left and right. Across frames 3–5, the head, shoulder, hip, and arm keypoints consistently show the man in right-facing profile, looking rightward into the breakroom rather than toward the camera wearer, with his arms hanging forward within arm's reach (<0.5 m) of the counter edge in front of him. The pose map infers full-body joint locations—including hips, knees, and ankles—through the solid wooden counter that occludes his lower body in frames 3 and 4, which cannot be seen directly in the RGB frames. However, the map is unreliable at longer range (missing the man entirely at ~4.5 m in frame 2), misses the partially visible second person at the right edge of frame 5, fails to render any magenta hand skeletons, and hallucinates a crouched, forward-bent torso and elevated legs in frame 3 where his lower body is occluded.
